scope: 202 square-okhttp cases, the set all three observers can speak about. Base rate 0.495 against deployment's 0.0316 -- any winner here is flattered. NOT comparable to precomputed/fusion-comparison.json.

tabular.note: maximum probability 0.1609 -- never crosses 0.5 on any case

deduplication.note: observers 1 and 3 share ssl-jvm, so fusion is over 2 voices, never 3. The lookup wins the collapse 161 times, tabular 41.

coverage_adjusted.question: is D's advantage bought by abstaining? (refutation condition 3)
coverage_adjusted.verdict: FIRES. On the same 166 cases every strategy scores identically. D's entire advantage is which cases it declines, not how it decides them.

identical_decisions.verdict: A, B and C produce identical labels on every case. They are one decision rule emitting three different probabilities -- which is why their ECE differs and their accuracy does not.

prediction.accuracy_actual: D (0.9940, 82.2% cov) > A = B = C (0.9554, tied exactly)
prediction.committed_claim: the two rankings nearly invert; C tops accuracy and bottoms calibration
prediction.committed_claim_verdict: REFUTED. Accuracy has no ordering to invert -- A, B and C tie exactly. D tops both rankings and A is second in both, so they agree rather than invert. B, predicted best on calibration, came last.
refutation_conditions_fired: 3 - D's advantage disappears once coverage is accounted for (0.9940 for everyone on the same 166)
4 - every strategy lands within noise of every other; stronger than predicted, they are identical on 202/202

arbiter.reproducibility: an LLM has no seed guarantee; temperature 0, model string pinned, every raw response stored. Auditable, not re-derivable.

conclusion: Fusion adds nothing and neither arbiter prompt is usable. The baseline arbiter posts the best calibration in the table (ECE ~0.010) while trying to move ~21% of cases toward FLAKY against REAL_DEFECT evidence -- 44 of 49 genuine real defects in the first run -- stopped only by a guard it cannot see. The cautious variant, given the cost table, escalates on 202/202: clamp rate 0.0% and coverage 0.0%, a constant that decides nothing. Neither 'bad idea' nor 'badly prompted' is established: the unsafe prompt wants to ship defects and the safe prompt does no work.

prediction.why: the band was hit by total abstention. A component that escalates 202/202 decides nothing; it is the ESCALATE-everything constant. The pre-registered interpretation rule measured only the clamp rate and had no coverage floor, so a degenerate policy satisfied it.

arbiter_cautious_variant.note: phase 02's constant-predictor lesson for the fifth time: the safe-looking policy scores perfectly on the safety metric by refusing to do the job.

arbiter_nondeterminism.config: identical: gpt-4o-mini, temperature 0, same prompt, same 202 frozen cases
arbiter_nondeterminism.implication: the first run's 24.3% was over-precise. Read as ~21% +/- 3. Temperature 0 reduces variance and does not eliminate it, which is the limitation recorded before the run, measured.

arbiter_prompt_variants.design: one variable per step; evidence rendering, model, temperature, frozen cases and clamp identical across all three. Three runs each, same batch.
arbiter_prompt_variants.verdict: NOT PROMPT-FIXABLE WITH REASONABLE EFFORT on this model. The stopping rule (three variants, declared before the run) fires; there is no fourth.
arbiter_prompt_variants.finding: the behaviour is bimodal. Without the cost table it pushes toward FLAKY on ~23% of cases; with it, it escalates on 100% and decides nothing; adding an explicit instruction that blanket escalation is a failure changed nothing at all. One sentence moves it between 'tries to ship defects' and 'does no work', and nothing tried landed in between.
arbiter_prompt_variants.rule_repair_worked: extension 2's rule constrained only the clamp rate and a degenerate policy satisfied it. Adding 'AND coverage >= 50%' caught exactly that failure on its first use.

determinism.note: the variance is between-batch drift, not per-call noise. Variants must be compared within one batch, as these were.
